SCOTT POLAR RESEARCH INSTITUTE
CAMBRIDGE
ENGLAND CB2 1ER
Tel. Cambridge 55601
13 September 1972
SCAR Circular No 292
To: National Committees
cc for information to: International Unions associated with SCAR, Permanent and Union Delegates.
Dear Sir.
Seventh Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting
In accordance with the usual practice of SCAR following a meeting, we are now in the process of correcting the reports of the Twelfth meeting of SCAR and complete sets of these reports (papers XII SCAR 33 to 44 inclusive) will be distributed within a few weeks. Summary versions of these papers will eventually be published in SCAR Bulletin.
At the Twelfth meeting of SCAR, statements responding to requests from the Sixth Antarctic Treaty Consultative meeting were formulated and approved as was a statement concerning "Specially Protected Areas". These statements are all incorporated in the reports of the meetings but in order that they might be conveyed to governments in time for consideration at the Seventh Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting we have extracted them from the reports and now enclose them separately. These are to be regarded as the official SCAR documents superceding those distributed in Canberra during the meeting.
I should be grateful if National Committees would convey copies of these papers (listed below) to their governments as soon as possible, with a request that they be considered at the Seventh Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting in New Zealand in October.
The papers enclosed for transmission to governments are:
Statement by SCAR on the use of radio-isotopes in scientific experiments in the Antarctic, being SCAR's response to Treaty Recommendation VI-5.
2 Statement by SCAR on Man's Impact on the Antarctic Environment being SCAR's response to Treaty Recommendation VI-4.
